solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chartered Accountant in condominium sadly unable to be contacted

indicators.note: in places the accountant's abbreviation inside the rearranged letters that follow
sadly suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of condominium are rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant holed up in a flat has unhappily gone off the radar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held incommunicado is cut off from all communication with the outside world.

clue.text: Letter from Greek island love cheers

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A letter sent from a Greek island full of love and good cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek island' looks like one unit, but Greek belongs with the definition and island is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth character of the Greek alphabet, the equivalent of i.

clue.text: Unite firm New Jersey supports with other industrial name initially

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
NJ is the US state abbreviation for New Jersey

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of other, industrial and name

explanation.surface: A business merger: a New Jersey firm teaming up with another industrial name.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjoin is to join together or combine, a formal synonym of unite.

clue.text: Deserve minor eyebrow raise at first — it's needed

indicators.note: at first tells us to take only the opening letter of each of the three preceding words

parts.note: the opening letters of minor, eyebrow and raise
it is taken as written; the 's is read as 'is', linking to needed

explanation.surface: Something so slight it only earns a raised eyebrow, yet it's still required.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to be worthy of or earn it, which is what deserving means.

clue.text: Pitiful, heartless — reform required to give boost

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the remaining letters are rebuilt in a new order
heartless means the central letter of the seven-letter word pitiful is removed

explanation.surface: A pitiful, uncaring organisation needs reform to give it a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitiful has seven letters, so its heart is the single middle I.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplift is a raising or improvement, as in a lift to morale, the same as a boost.

clue.text: Cerebral and popular, order European, punctual, to dismiss pun

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to tell someone to do something is to order them

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so the letters of the word pun are dropped from punctual

explanation.surface: A clever, well-liked, orderly European who is always on time but has no time for wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters removed sit at the front of punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone or something concerned with thought and reason rather than feeling.

clue.text: A team's digression

parts.note: a side is a team, as in a football side; the 's reads as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A sports team wandering off topic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark that departs briefly from the main subject, a small digression.

clue.text: Exaggeration about California, say, intended to be heard

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over something
California is an example of a US state, hence the 'say'

indicators.note: to be heard tells us we want a word that sounds like the synonym, not its spelling

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Someone makes a big claim about California, meaning it to be heard loud and clear.
explanation.definitionFit: An overstatement says more than the facts justify, which is what an exaggeration does.

clue.text: Number exercise, we hear, in part of plant

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: we hear signals a sound-alike: the syllable sounds like the training word but is spelled differently

parts.note: a drill is a training exercise

explanation.surface: A numbered gardening exercise on parts of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot a climbing plant uses to grip supports.

clue.text: Food, tons, ready to eat

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to be eaten

explanation.surface: Tons of food all ready to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as offal, especially in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is an edible offal, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Being of tender years, they, fun souls potentially

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Young people described as potentially fun-loving souls.
explanation.definitionFit: Youthfulness is the state of being young, which is what being of tender years means.

clue.text: In Mecca lend Arab table with date information

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follow it

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Mecca, all of lend and the start of Arab

explanation.surface: In Mecca, someone lends an Arab a table laden with dates, the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dates suggest the palm fruit in an Arab setting; the definition means calendar dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a chart or table setting out the days and dates of a year.

clue.text: Yearly warning unable to be ignored on regular basis

indicators.text: to be ignored on regular basis
indicators.note: ignoring letters regularly means dropping every other one, keeping the second, fourth, sixth and so on

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth, tenth and twelfth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A warning that can't be ignored, issued regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual means happening once every year, the same as yearly.

clue.text: Playing for fun, a pal you're texting

parts.note: a mate is a friend or pal
in text-message shorthand you're is written UR

explanation.surface: Messaging a friend about a game being played just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for pleasure rather than payment, unlike a professional.

clue.text: College is happily housing Japanese girl

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the answer is lodged within the run of words before it

parts.note: the answer spans the tail of College, all of is and the head of happily

explanation.surface: A college gladly giving accommodation to a young woman from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happily' looks like an anagram signal for 'is', but nothing is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained as a hostess and entertainer in traditional arts.

clue.text: Certain Mike is being included? A guess

indicators.note: included means placed within, so these letters go inside the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Is Mike in the team for certain? Someone ventures a guess.
explanation.definitionFit: A surmise is a supposition reached without firm evidence, essentially a guess.

clue.text: Busy type embracing conflict? Look out!

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: the bee is proverbially busy, as in 'busy as a bee'
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A busy person relishes confrontation, so stay alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware is a warning to be cautious, just like the cry look out.

clue.text: Around North Carolina, leave strange area unlike its surroundings

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the two-letter state abbreviation
strange signals that the letters of leave are put in an unusual order

parts.note: NC is the US state abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: Travel advice: when touring North Carolina, leave the odd area that doesn't fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory or community entirely surrounded by a different one.

clue.text: Noisily chew meat cut by Monsieur

indicators.note: cut by means split open, so the abbreviation goes into the middle of the cut of meat

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat, such as a pork chop

explanation.surface: A Frenchman slices a cut of meat, then eats it loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: M. is the French abbreviation for Monsieur.
explanation.definitionFit: To chomp is to munch or bite loudly, the same as chewing noisily.

clue.text: Article about ultimately fair English Cardinal

indicators.note: about means around, so the article goes round the letter taken from fair

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so take the closing letter of fair

parts.note: the last letter of fair

explanation.surface: A news article about a fair-minded English cardinal of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal suggests a churchman, but here it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a cardinal number, one used for counting rather than ordering.

clue.text: Controlled and guided herd of cows, maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of drive, as in steering a car or guiding animals
second meaning: a herd or flock being driven along; cows are one example

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from driving livestock: herding them along, and the herd itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Drove is both the past tense of drive, to steer, and the noun for animals moved as a group.

clue.text: A bad habit encompassing unlimited harm — greed

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the inner letters go inside the word for a bad habit

parts.note: a vice is an immoral or bad habit

indicators.note: unlimited means without limits, so the first and last letters of harm are removed

parts.note: harm with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A bad habit that causes boundless harm: greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, which is greed; it is also one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Journalist referring to hotel employee perhaps

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to
a porter carries luggage in a hotel; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A journalist writing about a hotel worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes news stories.

clue.text: Tidy, not using mixer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a spirit served ... has nothing added, such as tonic or soda

explanation.walkthrough: A mixer is a soft drink added to spirits, not a kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means orderly in appearance, and describes a drink served undiluted without anything added.
